topic: Will the periodic table ever be complete?

out_of_scope: nuclear reaction recipes or target handling
claiming element 119 or another element has been observed
providing IUPAC priority or naming judgments

subhypotheses.statement: Formal recognition of elements up to 118 does not prove a physical endpoint.
subhypotheses.allowed_conclusion: The institutional table ends at 118; the physical limit remains undetermined.

subhypotheses.statement: Future-element reachability depends on nuclear stability and technology/evidence together.
Discovery standards need method-aware implementation without lowering identity proof requirements.
subhypotheses.allowed_conclusion: Evidence contracts should be technology-neutral where possible.

subhypotheses.statement: An evidence-aware reachability model can be tested on historical outcomes without new nuclear experiments.
subhypotheses.allowed_conclusion: The proposed method can be benchmarked retrospectively and prospectively.

evidence_sources.citation: Hofmann et al., Pure Appl. Chem. 90, 1773-1832 (2018), doi:10.1515/pac-2018-0918
Hamilton, Hofmann, and Oganessian, Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci. 63, 383-405 (2013), doi:10.1146/annurev-nucl-102912-144535
Karol et al., Pure Appl. Chem. 88, 139-153 (2016), doi:10.1515/pac-2015-0502
Karol et al., Pure Appl. Chem. 88, 155-160 (2016), doi:10.1515/pac-2015-0501

evidence_limits: No source establishes a known maximum atomic number.
The documents do not contain a new reaction result or future discovery date.
The proposal intentionally excludes operational nuclear-physics procedures.
